A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research work, with 22 readable pages and complete Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIPOLE experiments on ExORL, OGBench, and NAVSIM, including numerical results in Tables 1-4 and 7 and ablations in Appendix D.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and autonomous-driving evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The greedified objective, positive and negative policy losses, guided action generation, and DP-VLA adaptation are unchanged, including Algorithms 1-2 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine ExORL tasks, 30 offline OGBench tasks, four OGBench tasks with online fine-tuning, and NAVSIM scenarios with navtrain/navtest training variants.

E2.justification: Tables 1-4 and 7 retain identical comparator sets, including CFGRL on ExORL, IDQL on offline OGBench, and DP-VLA fine-tuned with DPPO on NAVSIM.

E3.justification: The splits, model configurations, update budgets, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Both retain the same 1M offline/1M online update protocol and NAVSIM evaluation procedures in Appendices D-E.

E4.justification: The rejection-sampling comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity studies in Appendix D.4 and Figure 5, and driving case studies in Figures 2 and 7 are retained without revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions report main RL results over eight random seeds with standard deviations. Appendix D.4 retains its three-seed ablation reporting; no statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 4 retains PDMS scores of 88.3 for DP-VLA, 89.7 with DIPOLE navtrain fine-tuning, and 94.8 with DIPOLE navtest fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, policy decomposition, Theorem 1, and its assumptions and proof in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about stable, controllable diffusion policy optimization and applicability to large autonomous-driving VLA models.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix F's limitations are unchanged, including dependence on value-function quality and constraints imposed by reference-policy regularization.

D1.justification: Appendices D-E retain identical implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time disclosures. The project-page URL is unchanged and only relocated, with no added or removed access information.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to weighted regression, CFGRL, and policy-gradient approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint. Under review' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026.' The version stamp is updated, and the project link moves from below the abstract to the introduction's end; the prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The link relocation slightly reflows pages 1-2, and many formerly colored citation, cross-reference, and URL links become black. Figures 1-7 and Tables 1-8 retain their arrangement, content, and labeling.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same methods, proofs, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations. Publication/version labeling, project-link relocation, and visual styling changes do not materially improve or weaken the paper's clarity or scientific support.
